topic.title: How DNS Works Behind the Scenes

hook: Ever wondered what happens between typing a URL and seeing the page load? It starts with DNS.

slides.headline: How DNS Works: The Internet's Phonebook Explained
slides.body: Every website lives on an IP address like 192.0.2.1. Humans remember domain names; computers only understand numbers. DNS bridges that gap in milliseconds.
slides.visualSuggestion: Browser typing elevateweb.io translating into binary IP address packets

slides.headline: Step 1: The Recursive Resolver Lookup
slides.body: When you hit Enter, your browser first checks its local cache. If empty, the query travels to your ISP or cloud recursive resolver (like 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8).
slides.visualSuggestion: Browser Cache -> OS Resolver -> ISP Recursive DNS Resolver

slides.headline: The Hierarchical Tree: Root & TLD Servers
slides.body: The resolver queries the 13 Root Server clusters, which direct it to the Top-Level Domain (TLD) servers managing .com, .io, or .org extensions.
slides.visualSuggestion: Root Servers (.) -> TLD Nameservers (.io) -> Authoritative Nameservers

slides.headline: Authoritative Nameservers Hold the Final Answer
slides.body: The TLD server directs the query to the domain's authoritative nameservers (e.g. Cloudflare or Route 53), which return the final A or AAAA record containing the server's IP address.

slides.headline: Caching: Why Subsequent Requests Are Instant
slides.body: Every DNS record comes with a Time To Live (TTL). Your browser and local resolver cache the IP for this duration, eliminating external roundtrips for future requests.
slides.visualSuggestion: TTL countdown timer and local high-speed cache hit

slides.headline: Summary: DNS Powers Every Modern Web Request
slides.body: In less than 50ms, a hierarchical chain of four distinct server layers resolves human names into machine IPs. Follow ElevateWeb for deep-dive systems engineering.
slides.visualSuggestion: ElevateWeb architecture seal and systems takeaway badge

caption: How does your browser know where a website lives? Here is the complete breakdown of DNS resolution from root servers to authoritative nameservers.
